prologue.title: PROLOGUE: A WHISPER IN THE DARK

dialogues.speaker: Narrator
dialogues.text: The war against the Abyss had ended, and the kingdom celebrated its victory. Soldiers drank in the streets, bells rang across the capital, and the people praised General Joan for defending their homeland.
dialogues.rawText: The war against the Abyss had ended, and the kingdom celebrated its victory. Soldiers drank in the streets, bells rang across the capital, and the people praised General Joan for defending their homeland.

dialogues.speaker: Narrator
dialogues.text: Yet, behind the celebration, another battle had begun.
dialogues.rawText: Yet, behind the celebration, another battle had begun.

dialogues.speaker: Narrator
dialogues.text: Joan sat alone on the rooftop of his residence, watching the moonlight spread across the city. He had survived countless battles against the Abyss, faced enemies who wished him dead, and earned the respect of people who had once doubted him. Still, he feared losing the woman he loved.
dialogues.rawText: Joan sat alone on the rooftop of his residence, watching the moonlight spread across the city. He had survived countless battles against the Abyss, faced enemies who wished him dead, and earned the respect of people who had once doubted him. Still, he feared losing the woman he loved.

dialogues.speaker: Narrator
dialogues.text: Aflania had married him despite her family's objections. Their love had survived prejudice, distance, and the expectations of others. To Joan, she was more than his wife. She was the one person before whom he did not have to be a general.
dialogues.rawText: Aflania had married him despite her family's objections. Their love had survived prejudice, distance, and the expectations of others. To Joan, she was more than his wife. She was the one person before whom he did not have to be a general.

dialogues.speaker: Narrator
dialogues.text: A man climbed onto the rooftop and stood beside him.
dialogues.rawText: A man climbed onto the rooftop and stood beside him.

dialogues.speaker: Laqquo
dialogues.text: You seem troubled, General. The victory should bring us some peace.
dialogues.rawText: Laqquo: “You seem troubled, General. The victory should bring us some peace.”

dialogues.speaker: Joan
dialogues.text: The victory brings peace to the kingdom. It does not promise peace to the mind.
dialogues.rawText: Joan: “The victory brings peace to the kingdom. It does not promise peace to the mind.”

dialogues.speaker: Laqquo
dialogues.text: And what occupies your mind tonight?
dialogues.rawText: Laqquo: “And what occupies your mind tonight?”

dialogues.speaker: Joan
dialogues.text: My future. The woman I love. The things a man might lose without realizing they are slipping away.
dialogues.rawText: Joan: “My future. The woman I love. The things a man might lose without realizing they are slipping away.”

dialogues.speaker: Laqquo
dialogues.text: You should never place your love too deeply in someone.
dialogues.rawText: Laqquo: “You should never place your love too deeply in someone.”

dialogues.speaker: Joan
dialogues.text: Why?
dialogues.rawText: Joan: “Why?”

dialogues.speaker: Laqquo
dialogues.text: The deeper the love, the greater the betrayal.
dialogues.rawText: Laqquo: “The deeper the love, the greater the betrayal.”

dialogues.speaker: Joan
dialogues.text: You speak as though betrayal were inevitable.
dialogues.rawText: Joan: “You speak as though betrayal were inevitable.”

dialogues.speaker: Laqquo
dialogues.text: Not inevitable. Merely possible.
dialogues.rawText: Laqquo: “Not inevitable. Merely possible.”

dialogues.speaker: Joan
dialogues.text: Everything is possible, Laqquo. That does not mean everything deserves to be feared.
dialogues.rawText: Joan: “Everything is possible, Laqquo. That does not mean everything deserves to be feared.”

dialogues.speaker: Laqquo
dialogues.text: Forgive me, General. I speak only because I care for your happiness.
dialogues.rawText: Laqquo: “Forgive me, General. I speak only because I care for your happiness.”

dialogues.speaker: Joan
dialogues.text: Then care for it by giving me no reason to doubt those I love.
dialogues.rawText: Joan: “Then care for it by giving me no reason to doubt those I love.”

dialogues.speaker: Narrator
dialogues.text: Laqquo lowered his head, hiding a faint smile. Joan had not accepted the insinuation, but the idea had been planted.
dialogues.rawText: Laqquo lowered his head, hiding a faint smile. Joan had not accepted the insinuation, but the idea had been planted.

dialogues.speaker: Narrator
dialogues.text: Joan remained on the rooftop. For a moment, he considered telling Aflania about the conversation. Then he dismissed the thought. There was no evidence of wrongdoing, and he refused to let another man's suspicion become a shadow over his marriage.
dialogues.rawText: Joan remained on the rooftop. For a moment, he considered telling Aflania about the conversation. Then he dismissed the thought. There was no evidence of wrongdoing, and he refused to let another man's suspicion become a shadow over his marriage.

dialogues.speaker: Narrator
dialogues.text: He returned to his room, where Aflania was reading beside the window.
dialogues.rawText: He returned to his room, where Aflania was reading beside the window.

dialogues.speaker: Aflania
dialogues.text: You look as though you have been arguing with the moon.
dialogues.rawText: Aflania: “You look as though you have been arguing with the moon.”

dialogues.speaker: Joan
dialogues.text: The moon has nothing on you, my love.
dialogues.rawText: Joan: “The moon has nothing on you, my love.”

dialogues.speaker: Aflania
dialogues.text: Then tell me what troubles you.
dialogues.rawText: Aflania: “Then tell me what troubles you.”

dialogues.speaker: Narrator
dialogues.text: Joan hesitated. He could tell her about Laqquo's words, dismiss them as meaningless, or keep the matter to himself. For the first time that evening, he understood that what he did next might matter more than anything Laqquo had said.
dialogues.rawText: Joan hesitated. He could tell her about Laqquo's words, dismiss them as meaningless, or keep the matter to himself. For the first time that evening, he understood that what he did next might matter more than anything Laqquo had said.

options.text: Tell Aflania everything.
options.description: Joan is completely open with Aflania, seeking clarity together.

options.text: Dismiss the conversation and spend the evening with Aflania.
options.description: Joan bottles up his worries, attempting to preserve peace silently.

options.text: Ask Aflania whether she has noticed anything unusual about Laqquo.
options.description: Joan probes cautiously, inadvertently allowing suspicion to touch his wife.

dialogues.speaker: Narrator
dialogues.text: Joan sat beside Aflania and told her everything Laqquo had said. She listened without interrupting.
dialogues.rawText: Joan sat beside Aflania and told her everything Laqquo had said. She listened without interrupting.

dialogues.speaker: Aflania
dialogues.text: And what do you believe?
dialogues.rawText: Aflania: “And what do you believe?”

dialogues.speaker: Joan
dialogues.text: I believe Laqquo wants me to fear something I have no reason to fear.
dialogues.rawText: Joan: “I believe Laqquo wants me to fear something I have no reason to fear.”

dialogues.speaker: Aflania
dialogues.text: Then why does it trouble you?
dialogues.rawText: Aflania: “Then why does it trouble you?”

dialogues.speaker: Joan
dialogues.text: Because he is my comrade. I have trusted him with my life.
dialogues.rawText: Joan: “Because he is my comrade. I have trusted him with my life.”

dialogues.speaker: Aflania
dialogues.text: Trusting someone with your life does not mean surrendering your judgment to them.
dialogues.rawText: Aflania: “Trusting someone with your life does not mean surrendering your judgment to them.”

dialogues.speaker: Joan
dialogues.text: You think he intends to harm us?
dialogues.rawText: Joan: “You think he intends to harm us?”

dialogues.speaker: Aflania
dialogues.text: I do not know. But someone who truly wishes to protect you should be able to explain his concerns without asking you to condemn someone else.
dialogues.rawText: Aflania: “I do not know. But someone who truly wishes to protect you should be able to explain his concerns without asking you to condemn someone else.”

dialogues.speaker: Joan
dialogues.text: You are right. I will speak with him tomorrow.
dialogues.rawText: Joan: “You are right. I will speak with him tomorrow.”

dialogues.speaker: Aflania
dialogues.text: And until then?
dialogues.rawText: Aflania: “And until then?”

dialogues.speaker: Joan
dialogues.text: I will not let an unproven accusation change what I know of you.
dialogues.rawText: Joan: “I will not let an unproven accusation change what I know of you.”

dialogues.speaker: Narrator
dialogues.text: For that evening, they were at peace.
dialogues.rawText: For that evening, they were at peace.

dialogues.speaker: Narrator
dialogues.text: The following morning, Laqquo approached Joan with a new story: Cassian, a young officer, had been seen speaking privately with Aflania near the courtyard. Their conversation had concerned aid for families affected by the war, but Laqquo offered no such explanation.
dialogues.rawText: The following morning, Laqquo approached Joan with a new story: Cassian, a young officer, had been seen speaking privately with Aflania near the courtyard. Their conversation had concerned aid for families affected by the war, but Laqquo offered no such explanation.

dialogues.speaker: Joan
dialogues.text: You told me you had no proof. Has that changed?
dialogues.rawText: Joan: “You told me you had no proof. Has that changed?”

dialogues.speaker: Laqquo
dialogues.text: I witnessed nothing improper myself. I merely thought you ought to know.
dialogues.rawText: Laqquo: “I witnessed nothing improper myself. I merely thought you ought to know.”

dialogues.speaker: Joan
dialogues.text: Then you know nothing more than I do.
dialogues.rawText: Joan: “Then you know nothing more than I do.”

dialogues.speaker: Joan
dialogues.text: If you have a concern, present the facts. Do not ask me to build a conviction from your imagination.
dialogues.rawText: Joan: “If you have a concern, present the facts. Do not ask me to build a conviction from your imagination.”

choice.prompt: CHOICE 2A: WHAT SHOULD JOAN DO NEXT?

options.text: Speak to Cassian directly.
options.description: Joan seeks first-hand facts from the young officer directly.

options.text: Ask Emilia whether Laqquo has been behaving strangely.
options.description: Joan checks the credibility of his accuser via Laqquo's wife.

options.text: Confront Laqquo about his repeated insinuations.
options.description: Joan pushes back against Laqquo's subtle manipulation.

dialogues.speaker: Narrator
dialogues.text: Joan decided not to burden Aflania with Laqquo's suspicions. He put aside his worries and joined her by the window.
dialogues.rawText: Joan decided not to burden Aflania with Laqquo's suspicions. He put aside his worries and joined her by the window.

dialogues.speaker: Aflania
dialogues.text: You have been unusually quiet.
dialogues.rawText: Aflania: “You have been unusually quiet.”

dialogues.speaker: Joan
dialogues.text: Must a man always have a reason for silence?
dialogues.rawText: Joan: “Must a man always have a reason for silence?”

dialogues.speaker: Aflania
dialogues.text: No. But I know the difference between peaceful silence and troubled silence.
dialogues.rawText: Aflania: “No. But I know the difference between peaceful silence and troubled silence.”

dialogues.speaker: Joan
dialogues.text: You know me too well.
dialogues.rawText: Joan: “You know me too well.”

dialogues.speaker: Aflania
dialogues.text: I married you, Joan. I intended to learn.
dialogues.rawText: Aflania: “I married you, Joan. I intended to learn.”

dialogues.speaker: Narrator
dialogues.text: They spoke of the future they hoped to share: returning to the capital when the kingdom had recovered, and one day leaving military life behind. For a time, Joan remembered the life they had promised each other.
dialogues.rawText: They spoke of the future they hoped to share: returning to the capital when the kingdom had recovered, and one day leaving military life behind. For a time, Joan remembered the life they had promised each other.

dialogues.speaker: Narrator
dialogues.text: The next morning, Laqquo approached him with a more direct insinuation.
dialogues.rawText: The next morning, Laqquo approached him with a more direct insinuation.

dialogues.speaker: Laqquo
dialogues.text: I have tried to remain silent, General. But I fear you mistake my caution for indifference.
dialogues.rawText: Laqquo: “I have tried to remain silent, General. But I fear you mistake my caution for indifference.”

dialogues.speaker: Joan
dialogues.text: Then be clear.
dialogues.rawText: Joan: “Then be clear.”

dialogues.speaker: Laqquo
dialogues.text: Cassian has grown familiar with Aflania. Their conversations are frequent, and she seems eager for his company.
dialogues.rawText: Laqquo: “Cassian has grown familiar with Aflania. Their conversations are frequent, and she seems eager for his company.”

dialogues.speaker: Joan
dialogues.text: Cassian is an officer. Aflania cares about the people of this kingdom. They have every reason to speak.
dialogues.rawText: Joan: “Cassian is an officer. Aflania cares about the people of this kingdom. They have every reason to speak.”

dialogues.speaker: Laqquo
dialogues.text: Of course. Perhaps I am mistaken.
dialogues.rawText: Laqquo: “Of course. Perhaps I am mistaken.”

dialogues.speaker: Joan
dialogues.text: Perhaps you are.
dialogues.rawText: Joan: “Perhaps you are.”

dialogues.speaker: Narrator
dialogues.text: For the first time, Joan wondered whether Laqquo wanted to protect him or simply wanted him to believe danger existed.
dialogues.rawText: For the first time, Joan wondered whether Laqquo wanted to protect him or simply wanted him to believe danger existed.

options.text: Observe Cassian and Aflania without drawing conclusions.
options.description: Joan begins watching them, trying to verify Laqquo's words.

options.text: Confront Laqquo about his repeated insinuations.
options.description: Joan demands clarity from his subordinate.

options.text: Discuss the situation openly with Aflania. Return to Scene 1A and continue with Scene 2B.
options.description: Joan breaks the silence and confides in Aflania, then continues investigation with Emilia.

dialogues.speaker: Joan
dialogues.text: Have you noticed anything unusual about Laqquo?
dialogues.rawText: Joan: “Have you noticed anything unusual about Laqquo?”

dialogues.speaker: Aflania
dialogues.text: Unusual in what way?
dialogues.rawText: Aflania: “Unusual in what way?”

dialogues.speaker: Joan
dialogues.text: His manner. His words. The way he speaks of other people.
dialogues.rawText: Joan: “His manner. His words. The way he speaks of other people.”

dialogues.speaker: Aflania
dialogues.text: He is observant, but I have sometimes wondered why he seems so interested in the private affairs of others.
dialogues.rawText: Aflania: “He is observant, but I have sometimes wondered why he seems so interested in the private affairs of others.”

dialogues.speaker: Joan
dialogues.text: Have you ever given him reason to distrust you?
dialogues.rawText: Joan: “Have you ever given him reason to distrust you?”

dialogues.speaker: Aflania
dialogues.text: No. Why would you ask me that?
dialogues.rawText: Aflania: “No. Why would you ask me that?”

dialogues.speaker: Joan
dialogues.text: I am sorry. I should not have phrased it that way. I have no accusation against you.
dialogues.rawText: Joan: “I am sorry. I should not have phrased it that way. I have no accusation against you.”

dialogues.speaker: Aflania
dialogues.text: Then let us be careful about the questions we ask each other. Suspicion can wound even when it is not spoken as an accusation.
dialogues.rawText: Aflania: “Then let us be careful about the questions we ask each other. Suspicion can wound even when it is not spoken as an accusation.”

dialogues.speaker: Narrator
dialogues.text: The following day, Joan spoke with Emilia, Laqquo's wife.
dialogues.rawText: The following day, Joan spoke with Emilia, Laqquo's wife.

dialogues.speaker: Joan
dialogues.text: Laqquo has repeatedly suggested that Cassian and Aflania are too familiar.
dialogues.rawText: Joan: “Laqquo has repeatedly suggested that Cassian and Aflania are too familiar.”

dialogues.speaker: Emilia
dialogues.text: Has he?
dialogues.rawText: Emilia: “Has he?”

dialogues.speaker: Joan
dialogues.text: Do you believe he would deliberately deceive me?
dialogues.rawText: Joan: “Do you believe he would deliberately deceive me?”

dialogues.speaker: Emilia
dialogues.text: I believe he is capable of doing harm when he thinks he has been wronged. Whether he would deceive you is something I cannot yet prove.
dialogues.rawText: Emilia: “I believe he is capable of doing harm when he thinks he has been wronged. Whether he would deceive you is something I cannot yet prove.”

options.text: Ask Emilia to help discover what Laqquo is planning.
options.description: Joan requests Emilia's aid to investigate Laqquo's motive.

options.text: Confront Laqquo openly and demand an explanation.
options.description: Joan confronts Laqquo face to face.

options.text: Bring Aflania, Cassian, and Laqquo together to discuss the accusations.
options.description: Joan forces an open confrontation among all three.

dialogues.speaker: Narrator
dialogues.text: Joan found Cassian in the courtyard, reviewing reports about the families affected by the war.
dialogues.rawText: Joan found Cassian in the courtyard, reviewing reports about the families affected by the war.

dialogues.speaker: Joan
dialogues.text: Laqquo tells me that you have been spending considerable time with Aflania.
dialogues.rawText: Joan: “Laqquo tells me that you have been spending considerable time with Aflania.”

dialogues.speaker: Cassian
dialogues.text: I have spoken with her, yes. She asked about the condition of the soldiers and the people of the kingdom.
dialogues.rawText: Cassian: “I have spoken with her, yes. She asked about the condition of the soldiers and the people of the kingdom.”

dialogues.speaker: Joan
dialogues.text: Have you ever spoken to her in secret?
dialogues.rawText: Joan: “Have you ever spoken to her in secret?”

dialogues.speaker: Cassian
dialogues.text: Not with any intention of concealing our conversations. There have been private discussions, but nothing improper.
dialogues.rawText: Cassian: “Not with any intention of concealing our conversations. There have been private discussions, but nothing improper.”

dialogues.speaker: Joan
dialogues.text: You understand why I must ask?
dialogues.rawText: Joan: “You understand why I must ask?”

dialogues.speaker: Cassian
dialogues.text: I understand your concern for your marriage. But an innocent man may be injured by an accusation even when it is made quietly.
dialogues.rawText: Cassian: “I understand your concern for your marriage. But an innocent man may be injured by an accusation even when it is made quietly.”

dialogues.speaker: Joan
dialogues.text: You are right. I will not punish you for a conversation.
dialogues.rawText: Joan: “You are right. I will not punish you for a conversation.”

dialogues.speaker: Narrator
dialogues.text: Later that afternoon, a servant brought Joan a small silver butterfly brooch. It was the keepsake he had given Aflania on their wedding day.
dialogues.rawText: Later that afternoon, a servant brought Joan a small silver butterfly brooch. It was the keepsake he had given Aflania on their wedding day.

dialogues.speaker: Joan
dialogues.text: Where did you find this?
dialogues.rawText: Joan: “Where did you find this?”

dialogues.speaker: Servant
dialogues.text: Near the western corridor, my lord.
dialogues.rawText: Servant: “Near the western corridor, my lord.”

dialogues.speaker: Narrator
dialogues.text: Joan recognized it immediately. Aflania might have dropped it. Someone might have picked it up. Or someone might have deliberately placed it where it would be discovered. The brooch proved nothing beyond its own presence, yet Joan knew Laqquo would try to make it mean more.
dialogues.rawText: Joan recognized it immediately. Aflania might have dropped it. Someone might have picked it up. Or someone might have deliberately placed it where it would be discovered. The brooch proved nothing beyond its own presence, yet Joan knew Laqquo would try to make it mean more.

choice.prompt: CHOICE 3A: WHAT DOES JOAN DO WITH THE BROOCH?

options.text: Return it to Aflania and ask how she lost it.
options.description: Joan brings the keepsake back to his wife with honest concern.

options.text: Ask the servant who else had access to the corridor.
options.description: Joan questions the logistics of how the brooch arrived in the corridor.

options.text: Show the brooch to Laqquo and observe his reaction.
options.description: Joan tests Laqquo to see how he responds to the physical item.

dialogues.speaker: Emilia
dialogues.text: I must tell you something, General. But I do not wish to accuse my husband without understanding what he has done.
dialogues.rawText: Emilia: “I must tell you something, General. But I do not wish to accuse my husband without understanding what he has done.”

dialogues.speaker: Joan
dialogues.text: I ask for the truth, not a conviction.
dialogues.rawText: Joan: “I ask for the truth, not a conviction.”

dialogues.speaker: Emilia
dialogues.text: Several days ago, Laqquo asked me to obtain Aflania's butterfly brooch. I gave it to him because he was my husband.
dialogues.rawText: Emilia: “Several days ago, Laqquo asked me to obtain Aflania's butterfly brooch. I gave it to him because he was my husband.”

dialogues.speaker: Joan
dialogues.text: Did he tell you what he intended to do with it?
dialogues.rawText: Joan: “Did he tell you what he intended to do with it?”

dialogues.speaker: Emilia
dialogues.text: No. I cannot tell you what happened after I gave it to him.
dialogues.rawText: Emilia: “No. I cannot tell you what happened after I gave it to him.”

dialogues.speaker: Joan
dialogues.text: You have done the right thing by telling me. I will ask questions before I make accusations. That is what I should have done from the beginning.
dialogues.rawText: Joan: “You have done the right thing by telling me. I will ask questions before I make accusations. That is what I should have done from the beginning.”

choice.prompt: CHOICE 3B: HOW WILL JOAN USE THIS INFORMATION?

options.text: Confront Laqquo with Emilia's testimony.
options.description: Armed with Emilia's confession, Joan corners Laqquo with undeniable proof.

options.text: Speak to Aflania and explain everything he has learned.
options.description: Joan brings the truth back to Aflania to reassure her and clear the air.

options.text: Investigate the brooch's movements before confronting anyone.
options.description: Joan verifies the physical chain of events through the servants.

dialogues.speaker: Joan
dialogues.text: Your concerns about Aflania have become a pattern.
dialogues.rawText: Joan: “Your concerns about Aflania have become a pattern.”

dialogues.speaker: Laqquo
dialogues.text: I am attempting to protect you.
dialogues.rawText: Laqquo: “I am attempting to protect you.”

dialogues.speaker: Joan
dialogues.text: From what, precisely?
dialogues.rawText: Joan: “From what, precisely?”

dialogues.speaker: Laqquo
dialogues.text: From humiliation.
dialogues.rawText: Laqquo: “From humiliation.”

dialogues.speaker: Joan
dialogues.text: You speak of humiliation as though it has already occurred. What evidence do you possess?
dialogues.rawText: Joan: “You speak of humiliation as though it has already occurred. What evidence do you possess?”

dialogues.speaker: Laqquo
dialogues.text: I have observed their familiarity.
dialogues.rawText: Laqquo: “I have observed their familiarity.”

dialogues.speaker: Joan
dialogues.text: That is an observation. Your accusation is something else.
dialogues.rawText: Joan: “That is an observation. Your accusation is something else.”

dialogues.speaker: Laqquo
dialogues.text: You would rather believe them than me?
dialogues.rawText: Laqquo: “You would rather believe them than me?”

dialogues.speaker: Joan
dialogues.text: I would rather establish the truth than choose a side before I know it.
dialogues.rawText: Joan: “I would rather establish the truth than choose a side before I know it.”

dialogues.speaker: Laqquo
dialogues.text: You have changed, General.
dialogues.rawText: Laqquo: “You have changed, General.”

dialogues.speaker: Joan
dialogues.text: Perhaps I have begun to ask better questions.
dialogues.rawText: Joan: “Perhaps I have begun to ask better questions.”

options.text: Summon Aflania and Cassian to establish the facts together.
options.description: Joan summons everyone to the main hall.

options.text: Ask Emilia to reveal everything she knows about Laqquo.
options.description: Joan seeks Emilia's independent perspective.

options.text: Give Laqquo one final opportunity to produce genuine evidence.
options.description: Joan challenges Laqquo to prove his claims under formal scrutiny.

dialogues.speaker: Narrator
dialogues.text: Joan arranged a meeting in the main hall. Aflania arrived first, followed by Cassian. Laqquo entered last.
dialogues.rawText: Joan arranged a meeting in the main hall. Aflania arrived first, followed by Cassian. Laqquo entered last.

dialogues.speaker: Joan
dialogues.text: I have called you here because a serious accusation has been made, and I will not allow it to grow in secret.
dialogues.rawText: Joan: “I have called you here because a serious accusation has been made, and I will not allow it to grow in secret.”

dialogues.speaker: Aflania
dialogues.text: An accusation against whom?
dialogues.rawText: Aflania: “An accusation against whom?”

dialogues.speaker: Joan
dialogues.text: Against our marriage. Laqquo has suggested that your relationship with Cassian is improper. He has also implied that the butterfly brooch is connected to this accusation.
dialogues.rawText: Joan: “Against our marriage. Laqquo has suggested that your relationship with Cassian is improper. He has also implied that the butterfly brooch is connected to this accusation.”

dialogues.speaker: Aflania
dialogues.text: You suspected me?
dialogues.rawText: Aflania: “You suspected me?”

dialogues.speaker: Joan
dialogues.text: I have questioned what I was told. I have not decided that you are guilty.
dialogues.rawText: Joan: “I have questioned what I was told. I have not decided that you are guilty.”

dialogues.speaker: Aflania
dialogues.text: Then let me speak. I have treated Cassian as your friend and officer. I have never been unfaithful to my husband. If you possess evidence, present it. If you do not, stop using my name to feed your suspicions.
dialogues.rawText: Aflania: “Then let me speak. I have treated Cassian as your friend and officer. I have never been unfaithful to my husband. If you possess evidence, present it. If you do not, stop using my name to feed your suspicions.”

dialogues.speaker: Cassian
dialogues.text: I have served this general faithfully. I will not confess to a betrayal I have not committed.
dialogues.rawText: Cassian: “I have served this general faithfully. I will not confess to a betrayal I have not committed.”

dialogues.speaker: Laqquo
dialogues.text: You see how easily they defend one another.
dialogues.rawText: Laqquo: “You see how easily they defend one another.”

dialogues.speaker: Joan
dialogues.text: And you see how easily you mistake a defence against an accusation for proof of guilt.
dialogues.rawText: Joan: “And you see how easily you mistake a defence against an accusation for proof of guilt.”

dialogues.speaker: Joan
dialogues.text: Did you witness Aflania commit adultery?
dialogues.rawText: Joan: “Did you witness Aflania commit adultery?”

dialogues.speaker: Laqquo
dialogues.text: No.
dialogues.rawText: Laqquo: “No.”

dialogues.speaker: Joan
dialogues.text: Did Cassian confess to such an act?
dialogues.rawText: Joan: “Did Cassian confess to such an act?”

dialogues.speaker: Laqquo
dialogues.text: No.
dialogues.rawText: Laqquo: “No.”

dialogues.speaker: Joan
dialogues.text: Then what, exactly, are you asking me to believe?
dialogues.rawText: Joan: “Then what, exactly, are you asking me to believe?”

options.text: Believe Aflania and suspend Laqquo from his duties pending an investigation.
options.description: Joan places his faith in Aflania, strips Laqquo of authority, and protects the marriage.

options.text: Forgive Laqquo's suspicions but warn him never to repeat them without evidence.
options.description: Joan chooses passive peace, leaving the venom intact.

options.text: Remain uncertain and continue investigating privately.
options.description: Joan remains torn, continuing to search while distancing himself from Aflania.

options.text: Allow anger to overcome reason and accuse Aflania publicly.
options.description: Paranoia consumes Joan. He lashes out with public accusations, shattering his marriage forever.

dialogues.speaker: Narrator
dialogues.text: Joan returns the butterfly brooch to Aflania and explains what Emilia has revealed. Aflania confirms that she did not give the brooch to Cassian. Joan now has reason to suspect Laqquo's interference, but must decide how to act.
dialogues.rawText: Joan returns the butterfly brooch to Aflania and explains what Emilia has revealed. Aflania confirms that she did not give the brooch to Cassian. Joan now has reason to suspect Laqquo's interference, but must decide how to act.
